📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, latest reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

Sources indicate that the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

Industry observers note that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance Upcoming Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Newly introduced Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

In a recent development, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

In a recent development, this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Industry observers note that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no unveiled platforms.

In a recent development, although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is right now number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

According to recent reports, there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

It has been revealed that critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

It has been revealed that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

GTA 6 “Greatest Artistic Achievement In History,” Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.
  • Industry observers note that we don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion.
  • Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.

Industry observers note that we don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion. Most studios don't have that kind of change to throw around, because most studios aren't printing money with a game like GTA Online.

Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.

It has been revealed that "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he mused on Bluesky. "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

Industry observers note that "Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he continued. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.".

It's a sentiment echoed by others in the games' industry, like Larian Studios head of publishing Michael Douse, better known by his online moniker - Very AFK.

Industry observers note that "Maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to sh*t it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he posted to Twitter. "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!".

Naughty Dog game designer Michael Barclay even remarked that GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child.".

Considering, just three years ago, the industry warned that Baldur's Gate 3 was the game no other developer should try to replicate, given the unbelievable scope and sheer amount of interactivity, recorded dialogue, and branching paths it offered to players, that's one hell of an endorsement.

TheGamer's own Lead News Editor, George Foster, put it bluntly in his GTA 6 review, "we'll never get a game like it again," and frankly, we shouldn't.

Ballooning development budgets are already putting a target on studios' backs, making every single new release a financial gamble that could mean mass layoffs or even closure, and those high-stakes are only making the industry increasingly risk-averse.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 shouldn't set a latest bar for other developers to strive for. The unimaginable amount of resources, personnel, and time it took to develop the game is simply unrealistic for other studios. Thankfully, CDPR understands that. Let's just hope the rest of the industry does, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the significant fresh world headlining Version 4.0.

In a recent development, planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

According to recent reports, the Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Sources indicate that much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

It has been revealed that as you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two latest 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

Industry observers note that the other fresh arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

Industry observers note that when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

It has been revealed that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be revealed at a later date.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

Recent findings suggest that the Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

Recent findings suggest that the first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

Industry observers note that the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Sources indicate that heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

10 Best Games That Showcase The Xbox Brand

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has finally reached the momentous milestone of existing for 25 years, with all four generations of Xbox console greeting gaming memories that will last lifetimes for those who played them throughout the 21st century.
  • These days, however, in the wake of poor direction during the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S eras, Xbox is struggling to retain a healthy gamer population, with many gamers choosing instead to play games on Nintendo or PlayStation due those platforms’ vast variety of exclusive titles.
  • With Xbox having recently reached its 25th anniversary and the next generation of Xbox consoles, Project Helix, expected to debut in a few years, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive games that best showcase the Xbox brand and may potentially entice people to try an Xbox console.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has finally reached the momentous milestone of existing for 25 years, with all four generations of Xbox console greeting gaming memories that will last lifetimes for those who played them throughout the 21st century.

These days, however, in the wake of poor direction during the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S eras, Xbox is struggling to retain a healthy gamer population, with many gamers choosing instead to play games on Nintendo or PlayStation due those platforms’ vast variety of exclusive titles.

With Xbox having recently reached its 25th anniversary and the next generation of Xbox consoles, Project Helix, expected to debut in a few years, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive games that best showcase the Xbox brand and may potentially entice people to try an Xbox console.

Many fans of the British game developer, Rare, likely recognize them for creating Nintendo-centric titles like Banjo-Kazooie or Donkey Kong Country but under Microsoft’s ownership, one of the best games they ever released was Viva Piñata.

A life simulation game, Viva Piñata is set on the wondrous Piñata Island and has players restore a garden there with the goal of attracting, raising, and defending the local population of living piñata animals so that they can be eventually shipped off across the globe to become the center of attention at parties.

Viva Piñata encapsulates how creative, fun, and unique Xbox games can be and, while there hasn’t been a newly introduced Viva Piñata game in over 18 years, people today can still easily play it and other classic Rare games via the compilation Rare Replay.

One of the best games that showcases the absolute power and capabilities of modern Xbox consoles is Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, the latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series.

Like many flight simulator games, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 allows players to learn how to fly planes in both first and third-person but this game is the most advanced flight simulator yet as players can learn how to fly other real and fictional aircraft in numerous locations across the globe.

For example, people can fly Halo’s Pelican dropship over Yosemite National Park, the Goodyear Blimp over London, a DG Flugzeugbau DG-1000 over Mount Fuji, a Airbus Helicopters H225 over the Stilt Villages of Papua Upcoming Guinea and more.

Viva Piñata was very memorable but it wasn’t the most popular video game Rare made under Microsoft’s ownership, with that title instead going to the hit cartoonish pirate multiplayer game Sea of Thieves.

Played primarily in first-person, Sea of Thieves allows players to create and customize their very own pirate and ship as they set sail alone or with a crew of friends into monster-infested waters in search of treasure and glory across the sea.

Sea of Thieves might have had rough start when it first introduced in 2018 but in the years since, it has truly shined to become the definitive pirate multiplayer experience thanks to its comedic gameplay and eventful updates adding new areas to explore and supernatural sea creatures to fight.

For a while, Xbox was the best platform to play western RPGs on and, during the original Xbox era, one of the best exclusive games to showcase this status was Bioware’s legendary Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.

A third-person round-based RPG, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is set roughly 4,000 years before the events of the Star Wars films and follows an amnesiac warrior as they set out to stop the Jedi turned Sith Darth Malak from conquering the galaxy with the mysterious Star Forge.

While KOTOR’s gameplay hasn’t aged perfectly in the 23 years since its launch, its story, characters, and world designs have remained immaculate, with its characters going on to influence many other Star Wars stories and it still featuring one of the greatest gaming twists surrounding the character of Darth Revan.

Since the days of the Xbox 360, Microsoft has often invested and supported small game developers with immense potential, leading to the release of games like Braid, Ori and the Blind Forest, and the subject for this entry, Cuphead.

Studio MDHR’s debut title, Cuphead is a 2D run and gun game with visuals inspired by rubberhose-style cartoons of the 1920s and 30s, similar to Steamboat Willie, following the brothers Cuphead and Mugman as they set out to collect soul contracts from various bosses in order to save their souls from the Devil.

While Cuphead was only a timed exclusive on the Xbox One, it represents the brand’s ability to support small game development studios and uplift experimental titles into gaming stardom as Cuphead has gone on to sell millions of copies and become a highly successful multimedia franchise.

Racing has always been at the core of Xbox gaming from the early days of Project Gotham Racing to the more modern Forza Motorsport titles and while none of these games have been as popular as Mario Kart, one has managed to become the most advanced, realistic racing game yet: Forza Horizon 6.

The latest entry in the ongoing Forza Horizon series, Forza Horizon 6 has players take to the urban and rural streets of Tokyo, Japan in over 500 cars as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply explore the many beautiful landscapes of Japan alone or with friends.

In a similar way to how Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 became the premier modern flight simulator, Forza Horizon 6 has become the premier realistic racing game thanks to its hyperrealistic visuals, vast automotive and track customization options, and dynamic environments.

KOTOR is one of the best RPGs to ever debut on an Xbox console but it’s not the brand’s premier exclusive RPG, with that honor instead going to 2004’s Fable and the greater Fable franchise.

Originally pitched to be a fantasy RPG that would have allowed players to have kids in-game, and witness plant life grow among other promises, the original Fable wound up being a very charming, British humor fantasy RPG following a young boy as he set out to become the hero of Albion.

While the first Fable didn’t meet all of its creator, Peter Molyneux, aspirations, it sequels did slowly start to achieve all of Molyneux’s promises and more, becoming the source of many fond memories to the point that Forza Horizon 6’s own Playground Games is rebooting the series with 2027’s Fable.

One of the most recent games that best showcase the Xbox brand’s storytelling capability and multiplayer potential is The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day, the sixth mainline entry in the Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game.

Like its predecessors, Gears of War: E-Day is a third-person cover shooter with updated maneuverability but what made it really shine is its emotional story following COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they face the first horrifying Locust invasion on Emergence Day.

Gears has always been known for its gory, action-packed gameplay as well as its heartfelt story following people face seemingly insurmountable nightmarish forces and E-Day proves that Gears can still deliver horrifying, emotional yet hopeful gaming narratives 20 years after its first debuted in 2006.

The Xbox 360 era was arguably Xbox at its best and most successful largely in part due to Microsoft investing in several permanent and timed exclusive titles alike, such when Microsoft and Mojang worked together to make the Xbox 360 the first console home for the global sensation that was Minecraft.

While Minecraft was already highly popular on PC, Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition helped introduce millions of console players to the blocky survival game for the first time via Xbox Live Arcade in 2012 and led many to grow up with the game as it evolved and expanded with every update.

Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition’s success ultimately led to Microsoft acquiring Mojang in 2014 and since then, the two companies have worked together to make Minecraft one of the most successful multimedia franchises of all time through the release of numerous Minecraft updates, spinoffs, and adaptations.

The Halo franchise is as integral to Xbox as Sonic the Hedgehog is to Sega and Super Mario is to Nintendo and while there have been many fantastic Halo titles released over the years, I would argue that the best entry in the series to showcase the Xbox brand is the FPS prequel, Halo: Reach.

Bungie’s last Halo title, Halo: Reach has players embody the customizable Spartan-III Noble Six as they join the Spartan-II and III squad of Noble Team in defending the human military world of Reach from an alien Covenant invasion a few months before the events of Halo: Combat Evolved.

While Reach’s campaign is a ton of fun on its own, I believe Reach is the best Halo title to represent the Xbox brand because it remains the most complete Halo title to date as it launched with four-player campaign co-op, playable Elites, Firefight, Forge, Theater, Infection, Grifball, and more fun modes and features.

Toby Fox, the creator of Deltarune (and Undertale), has this week released his 'Fall 2026' newsletter, giving fans a "status enhancement" on Chapter 6...and Chapter 7.

According to recent reports, firstly, Chapter 6 is "progressing well", and the game is now a "structurally complete draft" that can be played from start to finish. In saying this, it will still take a "bit longer" to finish up some other scenes and details:.

"Much of the game looks complete… but, some key scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.

Industry observers note that as for the recent vote, Queen is officially the winner, taking out 65% of the votes. And the reward is a "stupid scene" from Chapter 6.

According to recent reports, and if this wasn't already enough, there's the Chapter 7 development update. The team has "only just started", and Fox has read out some of the events and dialogue to the team, but is withholding the rest of the story until they "complete more of the game".

I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.

Team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!

Fox ends the latest patch, reminding fans how the team has expanded since Chapter 4, but "more and more time is necessary" to keep the game's development going at the "fastest pace possible". The next update will apparently take place when the localization of Chapter 6 is done.

Industry News: GTA 6 Has an Easy Mode Buried in an Impressive Range of Accessibility Options

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.
  • Industry observers note that there's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable.
  • Sources indicate that but there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.

Industry observers note that there's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable. And while the initiative isn't quite as in-depth as what you'll find in recent Ubisoft or Sony-published titles, it's still a solid step forward for the studio.

Sources indicate that but there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows. As you might know, Rockstar never deals in difficulty levels; outside of things like adjustable aim assist, you're always in line with the developer's intended challenge.

In GTA 6, however, there are two difficulty-related toggles buried in the accessibility options: 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage'.

Recent findings suggest that in essence, both settings amount to having an easy mode. Accessible Combat decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.

Meanwhile, Reduced Vehicle Damage does exactly what it states on the tin, making your chosen ride more durable.

Industry observers note that but just how much easier do these toggles make GTA 6? The options menu itself issues a warning, stating that when enabled, the "balance and experience" of the game is "significantly" changed.

In a recent development, we've put them to the test, and despite some claims I've seen floating around the internet this morning, they do not make you invincible. You still need to play the game as intended — actually taking cover in firefights, for example — but the overall level of challenge is still noticeably reduced.

The idea is that these toggles will allow less experienced, mentally fatigued, or disabled players to progress without too much friction.

In a recent development, and just to be clear, enabling these settings does not disable Trophies. The bottom line here is that if you're having trouble getting through GTA 6, these options should almost certainly help.

Speaking of help, you can check out our overall GTA 6 guide and our totally spoiler-free Tips & Tricks guide for assistance with everything from collectibles to neat gameplay features you may not know about.

According to recent reports, as for the other accessibility settings on offer, Rockstar's covered a lot of ground. For starters, there are a bunch of aim assist and lock on options, while button taps and presses can be customised to an impressive extent, to make them less physically demanding.

You can even toggle "simplified" minigames, making the controls less complex, and there are multiple ways to customise controller layouts.

On top of that, a multitude of low vision options are available, there's a one-toggle brightness modifier, and there's a dedicated high contrast setting. Again, it's good stuff from the developer.

Have you been adjusting any of these options for your playthrough of GTA 6? Are you happy to see Rockstar adopting a more accessible approach? Snap to your target in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and now that NDA's have expired, actors everywhere are finally taking a moment to confirm their roles on the project through social media. The full cast includes a mixture of well-known names, traditional actors making voice debuts, and even a few who will note GTA 6 as their first major project.

In a recent development, of course, being as massive a release as it is, it should come as no surprise that, in addition to the main cast, a massive number of actors and celebrities are featured in supporting roles and cameos throughout the game. So, keep an ear out, because you never know where you might run into a voice you recognize.

Industry observers note that taking on the role of bank-robbing professional Raul Batista is none other than Manny Perez. Raul's chaotic energy and simultaneously suave manner couldn't have asked for a better voice to back it than this legendary Dominican actor.

Recent findings suggest that unlike some of the lesser-known actors you'll see on this list, Manny has a long history of work, including Washington Heights, La Soga, El Rey de Najayo. He has also had supporting roles in shows like Law & Order: SVU, Blue Bloods, 100 Centre Street, and Hawaii Five-0.

Manny Perez has also served as a writer and producer on many of the projects he has acted in.

It has been revealed that real Dimez is the iconic rap duo, Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, signed by Dre'Quan Priest at Only Raw Records. Voicing these talented women are actual Florida rappers, Hood Brat (Bae-Luxe) and Krissy Celess (Roxy). The duo has multiple tracks featured in the game, so needless to say, you'll be getting to know these voices quite well.

In a recent development, while Hood Brat and Krissy Celess aren't known for any other major acting roles and aren't a duo, you can find their individual music on major listening platforms like Spotify and Apple Music. So, if you're enjoying Real Dimez in GTA 6, check out some of their other work.

Dre'Quan Priest, voiced by Naiqui Macabroad, is a character you won't get to know until you've made it out to Vice City and engaged in the nightlife there, since he resides there while managing Only Raw Records and its newest talent, rap duo Real Dimez.

It has been revealed that though this is Macabroad's first major voice role, he recently made his debut as a prominent recurring character on Chicago P.D., so fans of the show will be getting to know his face well over the course of Season 14. Other notable projects include guest roles on demonstrates like Power and Law & Order.

A face you'll see frequently alongside Dre'Quan is Boobie Ike, a Vice City legend. He runs several things around the city, including the adult entertainment club Jack of Hearts, while also backing the recording studio Dre'Quan manages.

Voicing Boobie Ike is Mike Forbs, whose work has primarily been supporting roles across TV and movies up to this point. That stated, if his performance as Boobie Ike is any indicator, we'll likely be seeing Forbs' name on other major projects very soon.

According to recent reports, though you won't get to spend tons of time with Donnie, he leaves a pretty unforgettable first impression and plays a major role in helping Jason earn money early on. Voicing this man of chaos is Brad Carter, an actor with several guest appearances on highlights like Sons of Anarchy, Criminal Minds, Dexter, and Ozark.

A Few Supporting Voices As GTA 6 Locals That You May Recognize:.

Though you won't see Brian, Jason's boss, as often as some of the other supporting characters, you'll certainly be hearing his voice plenty when he calls with new orders. That voice belongs to Stephen Root, who you'll almost certainly recognize from one of his major roles. A few of those castings include Bill Dauterive in King of the Hill, Monroe Fuches in Barry, and Jim Hudson in Get Out.

While Lucia is a bit busy at the start of GTA 6, you'll quickly get to know Jason's closest friend and co-worker of sorts, Cal Hampton. Bringing Cal's laid-back persona to life is none other than Bobby Moynihan, who you may recognize from Saturday Night Live and a variety of voice work and traditional acting roles. Some of his most recent include Woody on NCIS: Origins, King George in Hoppers, and Louie in Ducktales.

Recent findings suggest that though you're introduced to Lucia right from the start, it'll be several hours into the game before she's a consistently present face and playable character. Voicing Lucia is Manni L. Perez, who you may not recognize from other voice roles, but might know from major guest roles on reveals like Law & Order: SVU.

That mentioned, Perez has voiced a couple of background characters in Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online, so if you're a major fan of the franchise, you might find her voice a tad familiar.

While Lucia and Jason are both playable characters in GTA 6, Jason is widely considered the primary main character, since you spend the first several hours of the game playing as him, and this Florida man is voiced by none other than Dylan Rourke.

Though you may not recognize this uniquely deep voice from many previous major projects at the moment, it's safe to say this will put Rourke on everyone's radar.

When you reach Rank 1 for any new Memory from the banner, you’ll earn a Memory-themed outfit with a special colour that matches your chosen love interest.

Illusio returns as part of the new event, too, letting you customise the look of Kindled Moments across all five new Memories. Things you can customise include selecting the outfits and accessories for each love interest, so you can recreate Kindled Moments in your own style. As always, Kindled Moments will go back to their default look after the event ends.

There’s a fresh mini-game to play, too, available only during the event. It’s called Courteous Fare, a frantic but familiar restaurant management simulation that allows you to unlock a variety of rewards.

8 Hard to Beat Game Boy JRPGs

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, back in the day we didn’t have a ton of ways to check how to beat something or find any guides that would be readily available.
  • In a recent development, even for some of the best JRPGs available you could spend a ton of hours just getting through one part.
  • Sources indicate that A lot of the games on this list are from series and part of that is because most games that released on the original Game Boy were not JRPGs as they weren’t quite as big in the states.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, back in the day we didn’t have a ton of ways to check how to beat something or find any guides that would be readily available. A lot of the time you just sort of muddle through until you figure out exactly what you’re supposed to do.

In a recent development, even for some of the best JRPGs available you could spend a ton of hours just getting through one part. It was a glorious time where conquering that challenge felt rewarding because of how difficult that particular JRPG section may have been.

Sources indicate that A lot of the games on this list are from series and part of that is because most games that released on the original Game Boy were not JRPGs as they weren’t quite as big in the states. Regardless, any game on this list is sure to give you a rough go of it if you aren’t prepared.

While Rolan’s Curse II is a bit more of an action-RPG, the game still takes several notes from JRPGs at the time and typically is counted amongst them. Instead of traditional turn-based mechanics, the game uses real-time combat making it more difficult than other JRPGs.

Many would go on to call it a Zelda-like game, but thanks to the inclusion of a party system with several characters it does fit the JRPG genre. The real-time aspect of the game made it more difficult to play, but also could force players into continuous encounters making things escalate in difficulty rather promptly.

Sources indicate that the original Rolan’s Curse is a bit different from the second entry since it doesn’t include a cast of characters to play as. Much as you might imagine the game centered around the same core principals although the upgrades and such are for your character.

Sources indicate that two things specifically make this one a bit tougher, one being that there’s limited ways to recover yourself and second the combat is fairly punishing. It’s a game that definitely requires you to play with focus and without that focus you’ll find yourself dying a lot.

The very first game to ever be released in the SaGa series, The Final Fantasy Legend has some interesting history behind it. The game featured fantasy and sci-fi elements alongside each other as players built a party to take on the challenge ahead of them.

According to recent reports, the difficulty of the game stemmed from how unusual the character development systems were combined with some harder combat as the game progressed. Players who didn’t take advantage of the systems for leveling would find themselves at an extreme disadvantage.

According to recent reports, despite the title of this one, it’s actually the first game in what would eventually become the Mana series. A much closer game to Zelda than many would imagine, but mostly thanks to weapons and such doubling as exploration tools.

It has been revealed that outside of that the game featured a party system in which an NPC could tag along on an adventure to help out. The real difficulty of this one comes from keeping tabs on your timing and positioning where even a small mistake could be costly.

A strange game for the time period that used a first-person view instead of top down for a fantasy JRPG. It took notes from things like Dragon Quest in terms of giving players the ability to investigate and engage with the world on a deeper level.

Since everything was fairly cryptic and there wasn’t much information given, players could often find themselves stuck on certain parts of the game. It took a lot more effort to get from one place to another if you didn’t want to do the investigating you had to.

This game changed some of the formula from the first one and introduced a tried and true JRPG mechanic, a party system. Rather than controlling one character the player now had a party to manage, but still used a first-person turn-based mechanic for gameplay.

Recent findings suggest that arguably a bit harder than the first game since now you dolled out resources amongst a party over just an individual. You could, of course, still miss plenty of things without investigating which led to players being at an extreme disadvantage some of the time.

Probably one of the crazier games in the series with a lot of going on in just about every part of the game. The odd fantasy and sci-fi bits of the game mixed gave players a lot of choice in how they handled leveling their character and gaining equipment.

It has been revealed that in true JRPG fashion, what makes the game unique also makes it incredibly difficult. By transforming your party members into various races based on items you gave them could really screw up your journey if you weren’t careful.

In a recent development, many JRPGs of the time period were doing some experimental work with various mechanics to spice up how their games played. Final Fantasy Legend II was no exception to this rule and even took it a step farther making it arguably one of the hardest JRPGs for the time.

Even the best JRPGs have some form of resource management, but those usually don’t apply to the story. MAGI, a collectible resource in the game, could be used to both enhance your character or progress the story forcing a difficult choice between power and story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the upcoming content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

It has been revealed that we know that Season 2 is introducing a major new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

Industry observers note that the real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Sources indicate that movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Sources indicate that audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

It has been revealed that diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

Sources indicate that the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

According to recent reports, the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the fresh class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

Industry observers note that war Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a fresh activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Recent findings suggest that echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first newly introduced class in 25 years.

According to recent reports, reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as fresh quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

#74900. Industry News: Call Of Duty Maker Activision Files Patent To Make AI NPCs Trash Talk

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (450 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Call Of Duty Maker Activision Files Patent To Make AI NPCs Trash Talk

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (450 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Call of Duty lobbies are synonymous with the worst recesses of the internet, a toxic minefield of abuse and harassment that's better left on mute.
  • As reported by Dexerto, the patent is called "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and describes using the audio from voice chat to make in-game NPCs sound more realistic.
  • The patent doesn't explicitly mention Call of Duty, but as Activision's leading franchise, it's a safe bet that's where it would end up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Call of Duty lobbies are synonymous with the worst recesses of the internet, a toxic minefield of abuse and harassment that's better left on mute. So, naturally, Activision has filed a patent that would train AI-powered NPCs to talk just like players do.

As reported by Dexerto, the patent is called "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and describes using the audio from voice chat to make in-game NPCs sound more realistic. It wouldn't copy your voice exactly, but what you say and how you react.

The patent doesn't explicitly mention Call of Duty, but as Activision's leading franchise, it's a safe bet that's where it would end up.

It would do so around 10 seconds before and after a flagged game event, i.e. kills, deaths, and losses, shaping how NPCs behave in the same scenarios. So, if players screamed every time they were trounced by a camper (as they often do), that data would be funneled into an AI model to make the most annoying Terminator.

The patent doesn't just mention in-game voice chat, however, but Discord and TeamSpeak too, meaning how you mouth off to your friends could be utilized in training AI models by matching timestamps across separate applications. I'm not sure that I want to hear Woods say he banged my mom, but if this patent were to go ahead, that's a disturbing possibility.

Industry observers note that abuse, slurs, bigotry, and the worst habits of anonymous gamers are a hallmark of COD lobbies, and that's why it's best to stay quiet and auto-mute everyone, if not disable voice chat outright. Training NPCs on that is a recipe for disaster, but the patent does note that it would include filters to stop offensive language.

According to recent reports, then again, AI filters have never been particularly effective. Just look at all the awful things people made Fortnite's AI Darth Vader say.

Of course, just because Activision patented this technology doesn't mean it will be implemented in-game.

Not only does the patent fail to consider the ethical quandaries of AI-generated dialogue and how it squeezes actors out of the creative process entirely — something that SAG-Aftra has repeatedly taken aim at over the years — but it makes no mention of asking for permission to use voice chat audio or the implications of using private conversations from third-party apps.

Industry observers note that reactive NPC dialogue is certainly an interesting idea, but using AI as a shortcut to shortchange actors and risking a breach of player privacy is one of the worst ways you could go about it. Maybe we should leave this patent in the filing cabinet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an awful lot of debate about the overall quality and lasting commercial success of Call of Duty across the last few years, with many arguing that the once unstoppable series is steadily losing its edge.

As such, this latest report from Circana won't make for easy reading if you're Xbox or Activision.

According to the ever-informative Mat Piscatella, the recently released Modern Warfare 4 was the best selling game of October in the US.

However, despite a strong debut and a mostly positive reception — especially with regards to its single player campaign — the big budget shooter has failed to break into the top 10 best selling titles of 2026 so far.

For Call of Duty, such an absence would have been unthinkable just a few short years ago; it really does suggest that it's struggled to match the kind of sales figures we've come to expect of the franchise.

Case in point: the current-gen port of Black Ops 2 remains on 2026's top 10 list.

Of course, there's still time for Modern Warfare 4 to make up some ground with the holidays right around the corner, but this seems to be a continuation of the downward trend that we saw with last year's very poorly rated Black Ops 7.

Indeed, it's possible that the Black Ops 7 backlash has negatively impacted Modern Warfare 4's appeal — and that's not the kind of spiral that Activsion will want to find itself in.

Elsewhere, Gears of War: E-Day — which was famously cancelled on PS5 just weeks ahead of launch — managed second place for October, and the eye-watering Star Wars: Galactic Racer entered in third.

Another new release, the largely fantastic Final Fantasy Resonance, landed in sixth — which feels like a win for Square Enix given the flood of games that came out last month.

* Projected digital sales ^ Actual digital sales.

10 Games to Play While Everyone Else is Playing GTA6

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, to say that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game of the year is a colossal understatement, with the game already pulling in billions of dollars in pre-order revenue.
  • Players could be waiting for a few patches before getting it for themselves (rather than dealing with any potential game-breaking bugs upon release), waiting for the game to go on sale (rather than paying the $80-100 full price), waiting for it to come to PC, or they may just not be interested.
  • Industry observers note that with that in mind, these players should have something to keep them occupied while others are diving into the huge title.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, to say that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most anticipated game of the year is a colossal understatement, with the game already pulling in billions of dollars in pre-order revenue. However, that doesn’t mean everyone is going to be playing it.

Players could be waiting for a few patches before getting it for themselves (rather than dealing with any potential game-breaking bugs upon release), waiting for the game to go on sale (rather than paying the $80-100 full price), waiting for it to come to PC, or they may just not be interested. Either way, there are all kinds of reasons that will keep someone from playing GTA6 despite it finally coming out.

Industry observers note that with that in mind, these players should have something to keep them occupied while others are diving into the huge title. They could play other games that recently came out, especially since this year has seen many incredible releases.

So while everyone else continues to carry the hype of GTA6, you can show other 2026 entries the same amount of love.

It has been revealed that if you were to break open any open world game to see what lives inside, you’d find a lot of the typical elements: quest-giving NPCs, tons of exploration, a healthy amount of combat and challenge. You get that with Crimson Desert if you were to crack open its world, but you also get some of the most unique expressions an open world can take.

The game is anything but a typical open world game, with zero slog to dredge through and an unparalleled approach to such a massive world. Seriously, as massive as GTA6 is, you’re going to be spending an equal amount of time (if not a little more) in Crimson Desert’s world.

This is one of those games where you need a good amount of time to properly sit with it, wandering the world and taking its challenge like a champ. It’s not like other open world games where you can get an idea of the world based on 15 minutes of gameplay, you’re going to need closer to 15 months before you can cement your opinion.

But I’ll just spoil the opinion for you: it’s going to be so, so cool, to where you’re going to actually be upset about it being snubbed at The Game Awards.

Industry observers note that if you grew up playing the Halo games, you’d be pleased to see that Halo: Campaign Evolved is everything you loved about them and then some. Not only is it an incredibly faithful remake for newcomers, but it also adds newly introduced content for veteran fans, meaning everybody has something they can properly enjoy.

Its singleplayer focus may be irksome for many FPS fans, but if you adored the original campaign, you’re in for the time of your life.

So sure, you may have waited 13 years for GTA6, but your inner child waited forever to feel that same magic from Halo again – and once you give the remake a chance, you absolutely will feel it throughout your entire soul.

Just don’t think about the current state of Halo, it’s better to live in ignorant bliss.

Silent Hill has been on an incredible winning streak lately, and it’s not looking to be stopping anytime soon, especially with the series’ newest entry. Silent Hill: Townfall is the most recent entry in the franchise, and it’s already carrying the torch (and tone) wonderfully.

Taking place in St. Amelia (a fictional island town in Scotland) rather than the titular town, you play as Simon Ordell as he goes through the tragedy of what happened there. Plus, you have to sneak around and hide to avoid monsters, a slight shift away from the typical survival horror tactics that the series has featured so far.

In a recent development, the entire game is an unforgettable experience from start to finish, with intricate and creative puzzles that will genuinely stump you and music that only amplifies your tense mood. Combine this with the incredible narrative (as standard for the franchise), deep characters (that too) and a new point of view, it’s a game that will stick with you.

If anything, if you’re a hardcore Silent Hill fan like I am, this game will just get you all the more excited for the upcoming Silent Hill Remake and future original titles.

It’s natural to feel protective over children, even in video games – but here comes Pragmata, putting you in charge of the child-robot Diana. You're not ready for the emotional bond.

As you and Diana explore the abandoned lunar base taken over by hostile AI, there are all kinds of things that you both can do: hacking, running and gunning, upgrading your abilities, teaching Diana the ways of humanity, and even dancing.

I just wish we could dance along with Diana; dancing is a joy that’s meant to be shared, and it’s far more fun to jump around with others, especially if we’re dancing with our robot daughter in space.

Recent findings suggest that but as you’re both trying to get out of space and back to Earth together, you’re going to feel warm and fuzzy at every interaction along the way. It's also just an engrossing, action-packed, and creative adventure, from a newly introduced IP.

Industry observers note that in the past few years, we’ve seen an increase in “dark wuxia” style of games, and Phantom Blade Zero seems to be our newest release in the subgenre. It’s an action game set in a literal phantom world, and you are armed with countless types of blades to help you along your journey … oh, and you’re also killer at kung-fu.

Devs describe the game as “kungfupunk,” and it’s honestly the perfect description of it. It looks good, feels good, plays good – it’s a fun time all around, with the added bonus of impeccable aesthetics from an alternate, dark fantasy version of China’s Ming Dynasty. It creates an action game that sets the bar, a upcoming standard for games to look up to.

It walks a delicate balance between a genuine challenge and action-packed fun, and players would be happy with the entire gameplay experience.

Combined with incredible cinematography, and we have a contender for Game of the Year that’s more than well-deserved. Regardless of what players believe the Game of the Year should be, I firmly believe that this game should win, at the very least, Best Action Game and Best Art Direction.

Fans of the first Control game have been eagerly waiting for a sequel that’s as good as the original, and that’s exactly what we get with Control Resonant. Instead of playing as Jesse Faden, you actually play as her brother, Dylan, as he tries to save New York from anomalies – but don’t worry if you were a fan, you’ll still see her.

Cool, action-packed and undeniably wild, fans of the first Control will be happy to see that the sequel kept everything they know and love, as well as adding so much more extra flavouring (and breathtaking graphics).

It’s a direct continuation, but amplifies everything to be just better than before, including the clear Stephen King inspiration. In fact, most players are going to find themselves liking this game more than the first.

Recent findings suggest that just saying, there’s a reason that it’s a contender for Game of the Year and several other categories – and I would honestly say that it’s more than well-deserved. It’s hard to live up to such a unique hype like with Control, yet this game seems to manage the impossible.

It has been revealed that while everyone is fighting against the police in GTA6, Gears of War fans have been fighting the Locust Horde for years; in Gears of War: E-Day, we see how this all begins. And if you’ve been a veteran Gears fan, you’re going to be pleased to know that it’s as fun as always – but then again, even if you’re a newer Gears fan, you’re still going to have a great time for entirely different reasons.

By coming to Unreal Engine 5, the game ends up going through much-needed revisions in the gameplay, especially when it comes to verticality. Yet, in spite of the adjustments, it’s still a great return to form.

Industry observers note that some players have complained about bugs and crashes, but they’re actually fairly few and far between, and most have been patched since its release. If one were to dive into the game now, the most they’d run into is Brumak deciding that a building is incredibly fascinating and needs a solid bit of observation.

With that in mind, this is an intense, yet super fun game that players will find a ton of time for, especially if they have been staring at it in their Play Later List.

Recent findings suggest that this year has been a great year for the Resident Evil IP, with a killer movie that continues to be gushed over by fans and this year’s fantastic leading title: Resident Evil Requiem. And, to be completely honest, this is my personal pick for Game of the Year.

Recent findings suggest that the game has you playing as two different characters: Grace Ashcroft, whose sections are the traditional horror experience that will have you genuinely terrified, and Leon Kennedy, whose sections are an action-packed power trip. Together, the two of them have to figure out the truth behind the newest virus, Elpis, and what to do about Raccoon City Syndrome.

Sources indicate that it’s action horror in the purest sense: a perfect balance of horror and action, yet maintaining a focus on the horror element first and foremost. It’s executed fantastically, and I don’t think I’ve ever had as much fun playing Resident Evil as I had with Requiem.

Sources indicate that if players were to compare all the recent Resident Evil titles in the modern era (including remakes), they’d notice something special about Requiem: it takes the best of all of them, and takes the crown as the best modern entry the series has seen so far. If anything, this makes me incredibly excited for what future RE games have in store.

It has been revealed that if you love Star Wars and XCOM, you’re going to be over the moon with Star Wars Zero Manufacturer. It’s a genuinely perfect marriage, a blend between the two that will have fans of both IPs weeping with joy.

If you’ve ever wanted to feel like the commander of a clone army, that’s exactly the experience that you’ll have with this game: but you’re not limited to having clones in your party. Your squad can be whoever you want, and you can implement whichever strategies you need to in order to be victorious.

In a recent development, many players might hear about these kind of real-time strategy games and imagine a top-down, board-like UI rather than anything more dynamic, but that’s not how it is in Zero Company. In fact, the game is incredibly cinematic, immersing you in ways that you normally wouldn’t be if it was any other RTS title.

Basically, if you’re looking for the game to have the ultimate nerd-out with, look no further.

Nintendo knows how to keep a loyal fanbase like with the Zelda franchise, and that grip has only gotten stronger with the recent release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

This remake isn’t like the 3DS ports that just improve what’s already there, no, this is a remake that’s rebuilt from the ground-up, and it’s just as incredible as we remember from our childhood. In fact, many fans (including veteran fans of the OG) would argue that it’s better than the original. Of course, there are purists, but purists will always have purist takes.

It’s hard to recapture the magic of the original, yet somehow, the remake manages to make the game feel even more magical, but with more updated gameplay (more reminiscent of Breath of the Wild) for modern players and better graphics. Seriously, what is not to love about a classic like this one?

Personally, I do think that Zelda can (and very likely will) outperform GTA6 at The Game Awards, because while GTA6 was easily the most anticipated game of all time, Ocarina of Time was, is, and always will be the most iconic game of all time.

Industry observers note that VL-7 psychoactive smoke appears to factor majorly into the gameplay of this newly introduced season, though we’re waiting to hear more details on that. We can expect new weapons, new gadgets, and the awaited return of the AH-6 Little Bird helicopter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

In a recent development, cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

According to recent reports, cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” says game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

Industry observers note that in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

In a recent development, mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest enhancement, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an problem that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Sources indicate that team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s upgrade takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Recent findings suggest that finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Industry observers note that hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the latest big content enhancement has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact.
  • This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps.
  • Industry observers note that the substantial fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the latest big content enhancement has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

Industry observers note that the substantial fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Recent findings suggest that varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

In a recent development, the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

It has been revealed that staying on the theme of reminiscence, the massive event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

According to recent reports, outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.
